strategy: flydsl_moe_fp8bs.py (gemm1) only, 3 knobs default-ON, all in _G1_KNOBS: FBS_PS_PRO=1 branches before the prologue so every padskip variant owns its X-tile-0 load + 2-deep B prefetch queue (35 spills/120 B scratch -> 0, 246 VGPR, full-body census = no-skip body); FBS_PS_SLEEP=8,12 adds s_sleep 8/12 at the end of every K tile of the 2-/1-subtile tail bodies (tails 0.85-0.9x of a full CTA instead of 0.71-0.80x); FBS_PADZERO=1 gathers padding rows' X out of range (zeros, no memory access). MECHANISM (measured with per-CTA timestamps): XCD == CTA id % 8 (100%); full CTA = 80-83K shader cycles, clock-invariant; unpaced 1-/2-subtile tails last 0.71-0.80x, finish ~14 us before their siblings, and widen the median same-panel sibling start spread from 2 us to 6-10 us (dispatch-rhythm perturbation of the one-shot grid). The 35 spills explain ~0 of the 2048 miss excess and ~30% at 4096. Sleeping tails let their co-resident CTAs run 5-11% faster, which keeps ~1/3-2/3 of the excess. Global lockstep proves the excess can be removed (misses at/below no-skip) but the enforced pace costs more time than ~1-1.4M misses (mostly MALL-hit re-fetches) are worth. Cache policy: nt on W13 loads costs 20-24% and nt on X 7% (L2 reuse across sibling CTAs is essential); all other bits are noise. For the TechLead: the remaining gap between the skip's MFMA cut and its forward gain is not recoverable by pacing or cache policy; the per-CTA timeline tool (FBS_DBG_TS in the NOT_A_CANDIDATE diff) is reusable for any grid-order/desync question.
